assessment.title: Self-check
assessment.intro: Answer honestly. There are no right or wrong answers, and your answers stay on this phone.

questions.moreThanIntended: I watch porn more often, or for longer, than I meant to.
questions.failedToStop: I've tried to cut down or stop and haven't managed to.
questions.preoccupied: I think about porn or urges even when I'm busy with other things.
questions.escalation: I've needed more extreme or novel content to get the same effect.
questions.harmedLife: My porn use has hurt my relationships, work, studies or sleep.
questions.coping: I turn to porn to cope with stress, boredom, loneliness or sadness.
questions.shame: I feel guilt, shame or distress after watching.
questions.despiteProblems: I keep watching even though I know it's causing problems.

assessment.frequencyQuestion: How often do you currently watch porn?
assessment.safetyQuestion: In the past two weeks, have you had thoughts that you'd be better off dead, or of hurting yourself?
assessment.safetyNote: We ask everyone this. If the answer is yes, we'll show you people who can help right now.
assessment.crisisBody: You deserve support right now. Please reach out to one of these services. They're free, confidential and there to listen. You can keep using the app too.

severityText.low: Porn has some pull on you, but you're in a strong position to change. Building healthy routines now will make that easier.
severityText.moderate: Porn is affecting your life and is hard to control. That's very common, and with the right tools and support it gets much easier.
severityText.high: Porn has a strong hold on you right now. You're not broken. This is a pattern many people overcome, and you deserve extra support while you do.

assessment.disclaimer: This is a self-reflection tool, not a medical diagnosis. If you're worried, talk to a doctor or therapist.

facts.title: Research & facts
facts.intro: Real findings from published research. New facts appear here automatically.

prevalence.title: You are far from alone
prevalence.body: In a nationally representative US survey, 10.3% of men and 7.0% of women reported clinically significant distress or problems from difficulty controlling sexual urges and behaviour.

icd11.title: It's a recognised condition
icd11.body: The World Health Organization's ICD-11 includes compulsive sexual behaviour disorder (6C72): a persistent failure to control intense sexual urges, leading to repetitive behaviour despite harm.

cueReactivity.title: Cues light up the brain's reward system
cueReactivity.body: In an fMRI study, men seeking treatment for problematic porn use showed stronger reward-centre (ventral striatum) reactions to cues that predicted erotic images. Avoiding cues really does help.

moralIncongruence.title: Shame makes it feel worse
moralIncongruence.body: Research finds that feeling porn use conflicts with your values strongly predicts distress. Self-compassion, not self-hatred, is linked to lasting change.

habits66.title: New habits take about two months
habits66.body: In a study of people building daily habits, it took a median of 66 days for a behaviour to become automatic (range 18–254). Missing one day didn't derail progress.

exerciseCravings.title: Moving reduces cravings
exerciseCravings.body: A meta-analysis found that even short bouts of physical activity rapidly reduce cravings. Exercise is one of the fastest urge-breakers you have.

urgeSurfing.title: Urges pass if you ride them
urgeSurfing.body: In a trial, a brief mindfulness technique called urge surfing helped people reduce acting on cravings. Noticing an urge without obeying it weakens it over time.

mbrp.title: Mindfulness prevents relapse
mbrp.body: Mindfulness-based relapse prevention led to fewer days of substance use and heavy drinking at 12-month follow-up compared with standard treatment.

sleepEmotion.title: Sleep loss weakens self-control
sleepEmotion.body: After a night without sleep, the brain's emotional centre (amygdala) reacted about 60% more strongly, with weaker control from the prefrontal cortex.

slowBreathing.title: Slow breathing calms your body
slowBreathing.body: A systematic review found slow breathing (around 6 breaths per minute) increases heart-rate variability and calm, and reduces anxiety and arousal.

ifThenPlans.title: If-then plans work
ifThenPlans.body: Across 94 studies, making specific if-then plans ("If I'm in bed with my phone, then I'll put it in the kitchen") had a medium-to-large effect on reaching goals.

lapseNotRelapse.title: A slip is not a relapse
lapseNotRelapse.body: Seeing a single slip as total failure (the abstinence violation effect) makes a full relapse more likely. Treat a slip as information, not a verdict.

socialConnection.title: Connection is protective
socialConnection.body: A meta-analysis of 148 studies found people with stronger social relationships had a 50% greater likelihood of survival. Isolation is a risk; connection is medicine.

peerSupport.title: Peer support groups help
peerSupport.body: A Cochrane review found that 12-step mutual-help programmes were as effective as other treatments and often better at sustaining abstinence.

gratitude.title: Gratitude lifts your mood
gratitude.body: People who wrote down things they were grateful for each week felt better about their lives and were more optimistic than those who listed hassles.

act.title: Therapy for porn use works
act.body: In a randomised trial, Acceptance and Commitment Therapy led to large reductions in porn viewing compared with a waitlist, and the gains largely held at follow-up.

protection.title: Protection
protection.intro: Make it harder to reach adult content in weak moments. Everything is set up with a tap and can be turned off any time.
protection.dnsExplain: Tap the button and allow the connection request. That's it. Adult websites will stop loading in every browser and app on this phone.
protection.dnsDisclosure: Android will ask to allow a VPN connection. Clarity Recovery uses it only to send website name lookups (DNS) to CleanBrowsing's Family Filter, which blocks adult sites. Your browsing traffic does not go through the VPN and nothing is logged by the app.
protection.dnsOnBody: Adult websites are now blocked. You'll see a small key icon in your status bar. That's the blocker running.
protection.alwaysOnBody: Open VPN settings, tap the gear next to Clarity Recovery and switch on "Always-on VPN".
protection.androidManualIntro: This version can't turn the blocker on by itself, but Android has a built-in setting that does the same thing:
androidManualSteps: Open Settings → Network & internet → Private DNS.
protection.iosIntro: On iPhone, the blocker is a free profile from CleanBrowsing:
iosSteps: Tap "Install blocker profile" and allow the download.
Open the Settings app and tap "Profile Downloaded" near the top.
Tap Install and enter your passcode.
Done. Adult sites are now blocked in Safari and other apps.
protection.webNote: The blocker works in the Android and iPhone apps.
protection.pauseWhat: When you open apps like Instagram or TikTok, you'll see a calm 10-second pause first.
protection.pauseDisclosure: To notice when you open a chosen app, Clarity Recovery needs Android's accessibility permission. It only checks which app is on screen. It never reads your messages, what you type or screen content, and nothing leaves your phone.
protection.pauseNeedsService: One more step: switch on Clarity Recovery in accessibility settings.
protection.pauseRestricted: Switch greyed out or showing "Restricted setting"? Android blocks it for apps installed outside the Play Store. Open App info, tap ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, then switch it on again.
pauseSteps: Tap "Clarity Recovery – Mindful pause" and switch it on.
protection.pauseNeedsBuild: The mindful pause works in the Android app.
protection.iosScreenTime: iPhone doesn't let apps pause other apps, but Screen Time can add a limit:
iosScreenTimeSteps: Open Settings → Screen Time → App Limits.
Tap Add Limit and choose Social.
Set a short daily limit, such as 15 minutes.
protection.partnerBody: Someone who gets a text when you press the panic button
protection.privacy: Protection runs on your phone. Clarity Recovery doesn't see or store the websites you visit.

instagram.title: Instagram follow check
instagram.heading: Clean up who you follow
instagram.body: Your feed is shaped by who you follow. This tool reads your own Instagram data export and highlights accounts that look like adult-content creators, so you can unfollow them.
instagram.howTitle: How to get your Instagram data
steps: In Instagram, open your profile → menu ☰ → Accounts Center.
Tap "Your information and permissions" → "Download your information".
Choose "Some of your information" and select "Followers and following".
Choose "Download to device", format JSON, and tap "Create files".
When Instagram emails you (usually within minutes), download the .zip file.
Come back here and tap "Choose file".
instagram.error: We couldn't find your following list in that file. Make sure you chose the .zip from Instagram (or following.json inside it).

box-breathing.title: Calm breathing
box-breathing.summary: Slow your heart rate and quiet the urge in 4 minutes.

steps.title: Settle in
steps.text: Sit comfortably. Drop your shoulders and unclench your jaw.

steps.title: Breathe with the circle
steps.text: Breathe in as it grows, hold, and breathe out slowly as it shrinks.

steps.title: Notice
steps.text: Let your breath return to normal. Notice how your body feels now compared to when you started.

urge-surfing.title: Urge surfing
urge-surfing.summary: Observe a craving without acting on it until it passes.

steps.title: Pause
steps.text: Sit down somewhere safe. Put your phone face down after starting this timer.

steps.title: Locate the urge
steps.text: Where do you feel it in your body? Chest, stomach, face, hands? Just notice — no judgement.

steps.title: Describe it
steps.text: Is it hot or cold, tight or buzzing? How strong is it from 1 to 10? Name it: "This is an urge."

steps.title: Ride the wave
steps.text: Breathe into the area. Imagine the urge as a wave rising — and you are surfing on top of it, not drowning in it.

steps.title: Watch it change
steps.text: Notice the urge shifting or fading. Urges always peak and pass when you do not feed them.

steps.title: Choose your next step
steps.text: Rate the urge again. Now choose something good to do next: walk, call someone, drink water.

body-scan.title: Body scan for sleep
body-scan.summary: Release tension before bed, when urges often hit hardest.

steps.title: Lie down
steps.text: Lie on your back, arms by your sides. Close your eyes.

steps.title: Feet and legs
steps.text: Bring attention to your feet, calves and thighs. Let them grow heavy.

steps.title: Hips and belly
steps.text: Notice your belly rising and falling. Soften your stomach.

steps.title: Chest and back
steps.text: Feel your back sinking into the bed. Let your chest be open and easy.

steps.title: Arms and hands
steps.text: Relax your shoulders, arms and fingers.

steps.title: Face
steps.text: Soften your forehead, eyes, jaw and tongue.

steps.title: Whole body
steps.text: Feel your whole body resting, safe and still. Drift off whenever you are ready.

self-compassion.title: Self-compassion
self-compassion.summary: Replace shame with kindness — especially after a hard day.

steps.title: Acknowledge
steps.text: Place a hand on your chest. Say silently: "This is a moment of struggle."

steps.title: You are not alone
steps.text: Remind yourself: "Many people fight this same battle. I am not alone."

steps.title: Be kind
steps.text: Say: "May I be patient with myself. May I give myself the kindness I need."

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe slowly and let the words sink in.

breath-prayer.title: Breath prayer
breath-prayer.summary: A simple Christian contemplative practice paired with your breath.

steps.title: Be still
steps.text: "Be still, and know that I am God." (Psalm 46:10) Sit quietly and slow your breathing.

steps.title: Pray with your breath
steps.text: Breathe in: "Create in me a clean heart, O God." Breathe out: "Renew a right spirit within me."

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Rest in silence. Hand your urges, worries and shame over to God.

steps.title: Amen
steps.text: Close with thanks for today and ask for strength for the next hour.

morning-flow.title: Morning wake-up flow
morning-flow.summary: 8 minutes to start the day energised, not on your phone.

steps.title: Child's pose
steps.text: Knees wide, big toes together, arms long in front. Breathe into your back.

steps.title: Cat-cow
steps.text: On hands and knees, arch your back as you inhale, round it as you exhale.

steps.title: Downward dog
steps.text: Lift your hips up and back. Pedal your heels gently.

steps.title: Low lunge (right)
steps.text: Step the right foot forward, lower the back knee, lift your arms.

steps.title: Low lunge (left)
steps.text: Switch sides: left foot forward, arms up, chest open.

steps.title: Standing forward fold
steps.text: Walk to the front, fold forward with soft knees. Let your head hang.

steps.title: Mountain pose
steps.text: Roll up slowly. Stand tall, feet grounded, palms forward. Set an intention for the day.

steps.title: Sun reach
steps.text: Inhale arms overhead, exhale hands to heart. Repeat slowly.

evening-wind-down.title: Evening wind-down
evening-wind-down.summary: Gentle poses to calm the nervous system before bed.

steps.title: Seated forward fold
steps.text: Legs out straight, fold forward from the hips. Breathe slowly.

steps.title: Supine twist (right)
steps.text: Lie down, drop both knees to the right, look left.

steps.title: Supine twist (left)
steps.text: Drop both knees to the left, look right.

steps.title: Happy baby
steps.text: Hold the outsides of your feet, knees wide, rock gently.

steps.title: Legs up the wall
steps.text: Rest your legs up a wall or headboard. Let your arms fall open.

steps.title: Corpse pose
steps.text: Lie flat and completely still. Let the day go.

urge-reset-yoga.title: 5-minute urge reset
urge-reset-yoga.summary: Move the restless energy out of your body.

steps.title: Shake it out
steps.text: Stand and shake your hands, arms and legs loosely.

steps.title: Chair pose
steps.text: Sit back as if into a chair, arms up. Hold and breathe.

steps.title: Warrior II (right)
steps.text: Wide stance, right knee bent, arms long, gaze over the right hand.

steps.title: Warrior II (left)
steps.text: Switch sides. Strong legs, steady breath.

steps.title: Tree pose
steps.text: Balance on one foot, the other on your calf or thigh. Switch halfway.

steps.title: Child's pose
steps.text: Rest forehead to floor. Notice the urge has less power now.

steps.text: Fast and steady.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Push-ups

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Squats

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Plank

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Lunges

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Mountain climbers

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Breathe.

steps.title: Cool down

walk-it-off.title: Walk it off
walk-it-off.summary: A 20-minute brisk walk outside — the simplest urge breaker.

steps.title: Get outside
steps.text: Put on shoes and leave the room. Being in public is a powerful barrier.

steps.title: Easy pace
steps.text: Walk at a comfortable pace and warm up.

steps.title: Brisk pace
steps.text: Speed up until you breathe harder but can still talk.

steps.title: Look around
steps.text: Name 5 things you can see, 4 you can hear, 3 you can feel.

steps.title: Cool down
steps.text: Slow down and head home. Notice how much calmer you feel.

grounding.title: 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
grounding.summary: Pull your mind out of the urge and back into the room in 4 minutes.

steps.title: Pause
steps.text: Stop what you're doing. Plant both feet on the floor and take one slow breath.

steps.title: 5 things you see
steps.text: Look around and name five things you can see. Notice colours and shapes.

steps.title: 4 things you feel
steps.text: Notice four things you can feel: your clothes, the chair, the air, your feet.

steps.title: 3 things you hear
steps.text: Listen for three sounds, near and far.

steps.title: 2 things you smell
steps.text: Find two things you can smell, or remember two smells you like.

steps.title: 1 thing you taste
steps.text: Notice one thing you can taste, or take a sip of water.

steps.title: Breathe
steps.text: Take three slow breaths. Notice how the urge has changed.

gratitude.title: Gratitude reflection
gratitude.summary: Shift your focus to what's good in your life.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Sit comfortably, close your eyes and breathe slowly.

steps.title: Someone you're thankful for
steps.text: Bring to mind a person who has helped you. Picture their face and silently thank them.

steps.title: Something in your body
steps.text: Think of something your body does for you every day, like breathing, walking or seeing.

steps.title: A small good thing today
steps.text: Recall one small good moment from today, however tiny.

steps.title: Carry it with you
steps.text: Notice the warmth of gratitude in your chest. Take it with you into the rest of your day.

desk-stretch.title: Desk & phone-neck stretch
desk-stretch.summary: Undo hours of screen posture in 4 minutes.

steps.title: Neck rolls
steps.text: Slowly roll your head in a half circle, side to side. Never force it.

steps.title: Shoulder rolls
steps.text: Roll your shoulders up, back and down. Then reverse.

steps.title: Seated twist (right)
steps.text: Sit tall and twist gently to the right, hand on the back of the chair.

steps.title: Seated twist (left)
steps.text: Twist gently to the left. Keep breathing.

steps.title: Chest opener
steps.text: Clasp your hands behind your back and lift your chest.

steps.title: Forward fold
steps.text: Stand, soften your knees and fold forward. Let your head hang heavy.

cardio-10.title: 10-minute cardio
cardio-10.summary: No equipment, low impact. Boosts mood and energy.

steps.title: March on the spot
steps.text: Lift your knees and swing your arms to warm up.

steps.title: Step jacks
steps.text: Step one foot out while raising your arms, then switch sides.

steps.title: Squats
steps.text: Sit back into a squat and stand up tall.

steps.title: Fast feet
steps.text: Run lightly on the spot, staying on the balls of your feet.

steps.title: Reverse lunges
steps.text: Step back into a lunge, alternating legs.

steps.title: Boxing punches
steps.text: Punch forward quickly, keeping your core tight.

steps.title: Skater steps
steps.text: Step side to side like a speed skater.

steps.title: Knee drives
steps.text: Drive one knee up to your hands, then switch.

steps.title: Squat pulses
steps.text: Hold a low squat and pulse gently.

steps.title: Cool down
steps.text: Walk slowly and stretch your legs and arms.

dietTips.title: Remember HALT
dietTips.body: Hungry, Angry, Lonely, Tired — urges are much stronger in these states. Regular meals are one of the easiest ways to lower your risk.

dietTips.title: Protein-rich breakfast
dietTips.body: Eggs, Greek yoghurt, oats with nuts or beans keep blood sugar steady and reduce mid-morning cravings and irritability.

dietTips.title: Go easy on sugar spikes
dietTips.body: Sugary snacks and energy drinks give a quick high followed by a crash — and crashes often bring urges. Pair carbs with protein or fibre.

dietTips.title: Cut caffeine after 2 pm
dietTips.body: Poor sleep is a major trigger. Stopping caffeine early in the afternoon helps you fall asleep instead of scrolling.

dietTips.title: Watch alcohol
dietTips.body: Alcohol lowers inhibition and is a common relapse trigger. If you drink, have a plan for getting home and putting your phone away.

dietTips.title: Hydrate
dietTips.body: Mild dehydration causes fatigue and low mood. Aim for a glass of water with every meal and keep a bottle nearby.

dietTips.title: Omega-3s and whole foods
dietTips.body: Oily fish, walnuts, chia and flaxseed, leafy greens and colourful vegetables support brain health and mood.

dietTips.title: Simple meal ideas
dietTips.body: Breakfast: eggs + wholegrain toast + fruit. Lunch: rice, beans or chicken, and vegetables. Dinner: fish or lentils with roasted veg. Snack: nuts, fruit, yoghurt.

sleepTips.title: Phone out of the bedroom
sleepTips.body: Late-night scrolling is one of the most common triggers. Charge your phone in another room and use a cheap alarm clock.

sleepTips.title: Same wake-up time every day
sleepTips.body: A consistent wake time, even at weekends, sets your body clock and makes it easier to fall asleep at night.

sleepTips.title: Wind down for 30 minutes
sleepTips.body: Dim the lights, read a paper book, stretch or pray. Give your brain a signal that the day is ending.

sleepTips.title: Can't sleep? Get up
sleepTips.body: If you're awake for more than about 20 minutes, get up and do something calm in dim light until you feel sleepy. Don't lie in bed with your phone.

sleepTips.title: Cool, dark, quiet
sleepTips.body: A slightly cool, dark and quiet room helps you fall and stay asleep.

sleepTips.title: Daylight in the morning
sleepTips.body: Getting outside within an hour of waking helps set your body clock for better sleep that night.
